data.name: Yatinraaj
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Yatinraaj is the name of the charioteer of Lord Indra, the god of rain and thunder. He is considered the deity of wisdom and is believed to guide and protect the devotees on their spiritual journey. Yatinraaj is a revered figure in Hindu culture, especially among those seeking knowledge and wisdom.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the spiritual guide and the journey towards enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: Yatinraaj is a compound name derived from the words 'Yati' (an ascetic or a mendicant) and 'Raaj' (King or Ruler). The name signifies a king or ruler over the ascetics.

data.cultural_impact: The name Yatinraaj holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, as it represents the charioteer of Lord Indra, the god of rain and thunder. In Hindu mythology, Indra's chariot is pulled by creatures called horses, but Yatinraaj is the one who steers it. He is considered to be an embodiment of knowledge and wisdom, guiding and protecting his devotees on their spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Yatinraaj holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism, as it signifies the quest for knowledge and wisdom. Yatinraaj is believed to be the deity of wisdom, guiding the spiritual seekers on their path to enlightenment. He is seen as a guardian and protector, and his name inspires one to strive for knowledge and understanding, both of the self and the universe.

historical_references.reference: Yatinraaj was a renowned Jain monk and philosopher, who lived during the 12th century in India. He was a prominent figure in the Jain Shvetambara tradition and is known for his contributions to Jain philosophy and literature.
historical_references.context: Jain monk and philosopher, Shvetambara tradition

historical_references.reference: Another reference for Yatinraaj is found in the 'Tattvartha Sutra' of Umaswati, an ancient Jain text. In this text, Yatinraaj is mentioned as one of the greatest teachers of Jainism and his teachings are considered to be highly authoritative.
historical_references.time_period: Unknown, but likely before 11th Century (as Tattvartha Sutra is believed to have been composed between 7th and 11th centuries)
historical_references.context: Greatest teachers of Jainism, authoritative teachings

data.spiritual_symbolism: Yatinraaj: The embodiment of divine will and master of one's inner world. Yati signifies a person who has renounced worldly desires, and Raaj refers to the king or ruler of one's own conscious mind and actions.
